Input: `main.nf` outputs in `results/`, GEO files in `atac_data/`, and SRA run tables in `metadata/`.
Output: `results/processed/`. Render with `quarto render analysis/preprocess_atac.qmd` from `atac_pipeline/`.

Studies stay separate. Each has its own consensus peak set, and Jiang (aorta) and Yu (retina) differ in tissue, so
no matrices are merged and no batch correction is run. Saved counts are raw and unfiltered, because `run_deseq()`
applies its own low-count filter.

Jiang's H3K27ac bigwigs (mm10) need no preprocessing and are summarised over windows in `DR Paper/analysis/pilot.qmd`.

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = "..")   # paths below are relative to atac_pipeline/
```

```{r libs}
library(edgeR)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(tidyverse)   # loaded last so its verbs aren't masked

processed_dir <- "results/processed"
dir.create(processed_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

cond_levels <- c("normal", "diabetic")   # same levels as DR Paper/analysis/helpers.R
studies     <- c("Jiang_2026", "Yu_2023")
canonical   <- c(1:19, "X", "Y")         # GRCm39 Ensembl names; MT is already removed by FilterBam

# Plan gates, pilot_multiomic_plan.md section P3
min_frip  <- 0.2
min_reads <- 20e6
min_tss   <- 5

read_meta <- function(study) read.csv(file.path("metadata", paste0(study, "_metadata.csv")), check.names = FALSE)
```

## 1. Sample metadata

Only the runs in `samplesheet/samplesheet.csv` went through the pipeline. For Jiang that is the C57BL/6J STZ arm; its
db/db, high-fat-diet and HUVEC runs were not processed.

```{r metadata}
sheet <- read.csv("samplesheet/samplesheet.csv")

# Aortic EC, so a labelled proxy for retinal EC. Never a retinal result.
jiang_meta <- read_meta("Jiang_2026") |>
  filter(Run %in% sheet$sample[sheet$study == "Jiang_2026"]) |>
  transmute(
    sample    = Run,
    study     = "Jiang_2026",
    organism  = "mouse",
    tissue    = "aorta",
    cell_type = "EC",
    genotype,
    model     = "STZ",
    condition = factor(if_else(treatment == "Streptozotocin injection", "diabetic", "normal"), levels = cond_levels),
    role      = "proxy"
  )
stopifnot(nrow(jiang_meta) == 7, all(jiang_meta$genotype == "C57BL/6J"),
          table(jiang_meta$condition) == c(4, 3))

# P16 retinal EC with no diabetes arm. Controls are the baseline reference; the Zeb1 arm is a perturbation.
yu_meta <- read_meta("Yu_2023") |>
  transmute(
    sample    = Run,
    study     = "Yu_2023",
    organism  = "mouse",
    tissue    = "retina",
    cell_type = "EC",
    genotype,
    model     = "none",
    condition = factor("normal", levels = cond_levels),
    role      = if_else(genotype == "control", "reference", "excluded_perturbation"),
    gsm       = `GEO_Accession (exp)`
  )
stopifnot(nrow(yu_meta) == 4, setequal(yu_meta$sample, sheet$sample[sheet$study == "Yu_2023"]),
          table(yu_meta$role) == c(2, 2))

sample_meta <- bind_rows(jiang_meta, select(yu_meta, -gsm))
count(sample_meta, study, condition, genotype, role)
```

## 2. Counts and peak annotation

featureCounts writes samples in arbitrary order, so columns are matched to the metadata by name.

```{r load}
read_counts <- function(study) {
  x <- read.delim(file.path("results/counts", study, paste0(study, "_peak_counts.txt")),
                  comment.char = "#", check.names = FALSE)
  cts <- as.matrix(x[, str_subset(names(x), "\\.bam$")])
  colnames(cts) <- str_remove(colnames(cts), "_filtered\\.bam$")
  rownames(cts) <- x$Geneid
  ids <- sample_meta$sample[sample_meta$study == study]
  stopifnot(setequal(colnames(cts), ids), !anyDuplicated(rownames(cts)), !anyNA(cts))
  cts[, ids]
}

# bedtools closest writes "." / -1 when a contig holds no TSS.
# ponytail: promoter is absolute distance <= 2 kb to the nearest annotated TSS; the active-TSS -2000/+500 window is P4.
read_peaks <- function(study) {
  read_tsv(file.path("results/consensus_peaks", study, paste0(study, "_consensus_annotated.bed")),
           col_names = c("chr", "start", "end", "tss_chr", "tss_start", "tss_end",
                         "gene_id", "gene_name", "strand", "distance_to_tss"),
           col_types = "ciiciicccd", na = ".") |>
    mutate(peak_id = paste0(chr, ":", start, "-", end),
           distance_to_tss = na_if(distance_to_tss, -1),
           peak_class = if_else(!is.na(distance_to_tss) & distance_to_tss <= 2000, "promoter", "distal")) |>
    select(peak_id, chr, start, end, gene_id, gene_name, strand, distance_to_tss, peak_class)
}

# Peaks on unplaced contigs are dropped. Coordinates are BED (0-based start), as in peak_id.
counts <- map(set_names(studies), read_counts)
peaks  <- map(set_names(studies), \(s) {
  p <- read_peaks(s)
  stopifnot(setequal(p$peak_id, rownames(counts[[s]])), !anyDuplicated(p$peak_id))
  filter(p, chr %in% canonical)
})
counts <- imap(counts, \(cts, s) cts[peaks[[s]]$peak_id, ])

imap_dfr(peaks, \(p, s) tibble(study = s, peaks = nrow(p), promoter = sum(p$peak_class == "promoter"),
                               median_width = median(p$end - p$start)))
```

## 3. QC against the plan gates

FRiP and the read count come from the featureCounts summary, so they describe the filtered BAM: nuclear, MAPQ >= 30,
properly paired, deduplicated. Pairs are doubled to reads. FRiP uses the same denominator as `update_master_sheet.py`.
It is calculated on the study's own consensus peaks, before contigs are dropped.

`tss_enrichment` is `NA` because the pipeline doesn't compute it. A sample therefore reads `fail` or `pending_tss`,
never `pass`.

```{r qc}
mqc <- function(study, file) {
  read.delim(file.path("results/multiqc", study, paste0(study, "_multiqc_report_data"), file), check.names = FALSE) |>
    mutate(sample = str_remove(Sample, "_.*$"))
}

study_qc <- function(study) {
  summ <- read.delim(file.path("results/counts", study, paste0(study, "_peak_counts.txt.summary")), check.names = FALSE) |>
    pivot_longer(-Status, names_to = "sample", values_to = "n") |>
    mutate(sample = str_remove(sample, "_filtered\\.bam$")) |>
    summarise(frip = sum(n[Status == "Assigned"]) / sum(n), filtered_reads = 2 * sum(n), .by = sample)

  summ |>
    left_join(transmute(mqc(study, "multiqc_macs.txt"), sample, macs_peaks = peak_count), by = "sample") |>
    left_join(transmute(mqc(study, "multiqc_bowtie2.txt"), sample, align_rate = overall_alignment_rate), by = "sample") |>
    left_join(transmute(mqc(study, "multiqc_picard_dups.txt"), sample, pct_dup = 100 * PERCENT_DUPLICATION), by = "sample") |>
    left_join(transmute(mqc(study, "multiqc_samtools_stats.txt"), sample, mean_insert = insert_size_average), by = "sample")
}

sample_qc <- map_dfr(studies, study_qc) |>
  mutate(tss_enrichment = NA_real_,
         frip_ok  = frip >= min_frip,
         reads_ok = filtered_reads >= min_reads,
         gate     = if_else(frip_ok & reads_ok, "pending_tss", "fail"))

sample_meta <- left_join(sample_meta, sample_qc, by = "sample")
stopifnot(!anyNA(select(sample_meta, frip, macs_peaks, align_rate, pct_dup, mean_insert)))

sample_meta |>
  select(study, sample, condition, genotype, frip, filtered_reads, macs_peaks, align_rate, pct_dup, mean_insert, gate) |>
  mutate(across(c(frip), \(x) round(x, 3)), filtered_reads = round(filtered_reads / 1e6, 1)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## 4. PCA

Log-CPM on the top 2,000 most variable peaks, after the same low-count rule as `run_deseq()`. Labels show MACS3 peak
counts, to separate biology from library quality.

```{r pca, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4}
study_pca <- function(study) {
  m   <- filter(sample_meta, study == !!study) |> mutate(group = interaction(condition, genotype, drop = TRUE))
  cts <- counts[[study]][, m$sample]
  keep <- rowSums(cts >= 10) >= min(table(m$group))
  lcpm <- cpm(cts[keep, ], log = TRUE)
  top  <- head(order(apply(lcpm, 1, var), decreasing = TRUE), 2000)
  pc   <- prcomp(t(lcpm[top, ]))
  pv   <- round(100 * pc$sdev^2 / sum(pc$sdev^2))
  bind_cols(m, as_tibble(pc$x[, 1:2])) |>
    mutate(panel = sprintf("%s (%d/%d peaks kept; PC1 %d%%, PC2 %d%%)", study, sum(keep), nrow(cts), pv[1], pv[2]))
}

map_dfr(studies, study_pca) |>
  ggplot(aes(PC1, PC2, colour = group, label = macs_peaks)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_text(vjust = -0.8, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw()
```

## 5. Published peak sets

Reference sets only, called by the original authors and never counted.

**Yuan 2026:** healthy human multiome, 1 bp summits per cell type. Build taken as hg38 and still marked `VERIFY` in
the plan. Sets under 5,000 summits are flagged `low_peak_count`. `Perictyes` is a typo in the GEO filename, corrected
in the label only.

**Yu 2023 GEO:** these are **not on GRCm39**, so don't overlap them with pipeline peaks without a liftOver. The `chr`
prefix alone doesn't explain it (see the check below). Use the Yu consensus from section 2 for GRCm39 work.

```{r reference-peaks}
yuan_files <- list.files("atac_data/Yuan_2026", "summits_filter\\.bed\\.gz$", full.names = TRUE)
yuan <- map_dfr(yuan_files, \(f) {
  read_tsv(f, col_names = c("chr", "start", "end", "name", "score"), col_types = "ciicd") |>
    mutate(cell_type = str_match(basename(f), "GSE277326_(.+)_0\\.\\d+_summits")[, 2],
           summit_cutoff = as.numeric(str_match(basename(f), "_(0\\.\\d+)_summits")[, 2]))
}) |>
  mutate(cell_type = str_replace(cell_type, "Perictyes", "Pericytes"),
         low_peak_count = n() < 5000, .by = cell_type)
stopifnot(n_distinct(yuan$cell_type) == length(yuan_files), all(yuan$end - yuan$start == 1))

yu_files <- list.files("atac_data/Yu_2023", "broadPeak\\.gz$", full.names = TRUE)
yu_geo <- map_dfr(yu_files, \(f) {
  read_tsv(f, col_names = c("chr", "start", "end", "name", "score", "strand", "signal", "p", "q"),
           col_types = "ciicicddd", na = ".") |>
    mutate(gsm = str_extract(basename(f), "^GSM\\d+"))
}) |>
  left_join(select(yu_meta, gsm, sample, genotype, role), by = "gsm")
stopifnot(!anyNA(yu_geo$sample), n_distinct(yu_geo$sample) == 4)

as_gr <- function(x, genome) {
  gr <- makeGRangesFromDataFrame(x, keep.extra.columns = TRUE, starts.in.df.are.0based = TRUE)
  gr$genome <- genome
  gr
}
reference_peaks <- list(
  yuan   = as_gr(yuan, "hg38 (VERIFY)"),
  yu_geo = as_gr(select(yu_geo, -strand), "older than GRCm39 (likely mm10)")
)

count(yuan, cell_type, low_peak_count, name = "summits")
```

### Build check for the GEO Yu peaks

If the GEO peaks were on GRCm39, most would overlap the consensus at their stated coordinates. A build difference
shows up as low overlap that recovers once the coordinates are offset.

```{r yu-build-check}
yu_cons <- GRanges(paste0("chr", peaks$Yu_2023$chr), IRanges(peaks$Yu_2023$start + 1, peaks$Yu_2023$end))
yu_all <- reference_peaks$yu_geo

direct <- mean(overlapsAny(yu_all, yu_cons))

# Offsets between builds change along a chromosome, so sweep one narrow stretch of chr1.
stretch <- yu_all[seqnames(yu_all) == "chr1" & start(yu_all) < 30e6]
sweep <- tibble(offset = seq(-300e3, 300e3, by = 1e3)) |>
  mutate(overlap = map_dbl(offset, \(o) mean(overlapsAny(shift(stretch, o), yu_cons))))
best <- slice_max(sweep, overlap, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

tibble(direct_overlap_all = direct,
       chr1_stretch_at_0 = sweep$overlap[sweep$offset == 0],
       chr1_stretch_best = best$overlap,
       best_offset = best$offset)
```

## 6. Save

```{r save}
iwalk(counts, \(cts, s) saveRDS(cts, file.path(processed_dir, paste0(s, "_peak_counts.rds"))))
iwalk(peaks,  \(p, s) write_csv(p, file.path(processed_dir, paste0(s, "_peaks.csv"))))
write_csv(sample_meta, file.path(processed_dir, "atac_sample_metadata.csv"))
saveRDS(reference_peaks, file.path(processed_dir, "atac_reference_peaks.rds"))

# Reload what was written, so a downstream load_cohort()-style check holds
walk(studies, \(s) {
  cts <- readRDS(file.path(processed_dir, paste0(s, "_peak_counts.rds")))
  m   <- read.csv(file.path(processed_dir, "atac_sample_metadata.csv")) |> filter(study == s)
  p   <- read.csv(file.path(processed_dir, paste0(s, "_peaks.csv")), colClasses = c(chr = "character"))
  stopifnot(identical(colnames(cts), m$sample), identical(rownames(cts), p$peak_id))
})
list.files(processed_dir)
```
